items.q: Management STEP 2 is:
items.exp: STEP 2: EPO stimulating agents (ESA). (Book p810)

items.q: The prerequisite TSAT to start EPO is:
items.exp: Prerequisite to start EPO: TSAT ≥30%. (Book p810)

items.q: The prerequisite serum ferritin to start EPO is:
items.exp: Prerequisite: s. ferritin ≥500 ng/ml. (Book p810)

items.q: The two prerequisites to start EPO, bracketed as 'enough iron store', are:
items.exp: Prerequisite to start EPO: TSAT ≥30%, s. ferritin ≥500 ng/ml → enough iron store. (Book p810)

items.q: The absolute contraindication to ESA listed is:
items.exp: Contraindications: absolute — stroke; relative — malignancy. (Book p810)

items.q: The relative contraindication to ESA listed is:
items.exp: Relative: malignancy. (Book p810)

items.q: The preferred ESA route, SC, requires how much less dose?
items.exp: Route: SC (preferred) — 30% less dose required. (Book p810)

items.q: The half-life of first-generation EPO-α (recombinant human erythropoietin) is:
items.exp: EPO-α: T½ 8.5 hrs. (Book p810)

items.q: The starting EPO-α dose is:
items.exp: 50-100 U/kg/week or 4000-10000 U/week; increase dose up to 300 U/kg/week. (Book p810)

items.q: The EPO-α dose can be increased up to:
items.exp: Increase dose up to 300 U/kg/week. (Book p810)

items.q: No response to ESA is labelled:
items.exp: No response: ESA hyporesponsiveness. (Book p810)

items.q: The most common cause of ESA hyporesponsiveness is:
items.exp: Cause: iron deficiency (m/c), chronic disease. (Book p810)

items.q: All but one appear in the ESA drug block. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The ESA block lists daprodustat (newer drug), darbepoetin α and EPO-β (CERA). (Book p810)

items.q: Daprodustat's mechanism of action is:
items.exp: Daprodustat: MOA — prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor; route oral; limitations — high cost. (Book p810)

items.q: Daprodustat is given by the IV route.
items.exp: Route: oral. (Book p810)

items.q: Fill up: Second-generation ESAs carry two extra ______-linked glycosylation chains.
items.exp: 2nd generation: (2 extra N-linked glycosylation chains). (Book p810)

items.q: Match the following ESA to its half-life — 1) EPO-α  2) Darbepoetin α  3) EPO-β (CERA) … A) 25.3 hrs  B) 8.5 hrs  C) 130 hrs
items.exp: T½: EPO-α 8.5 hrs; darbepoetin α 25.3 hrs; CERA 130 hrs. (Book p810)

items.q: Darbepoetin α is dosed at:
items.exp: Darbepoetin α: T½ 25.3 hrs; 60-200 µg/2 weekly. (Book p810)

items.q: CERA (EPO-β / methoxy polyethylene glycol-β) is dosed at:
items.exp: EPO-β (CERA): T½ 130 hrs; 0.6 µg/kg/2 weekly. (Book p810)

items.q: A CKD patient with Hb 10.2 g/dl, TSAT 22% and ferritin 380 ng/ml wants to start an ESA. The correct next step is:
opts: Replenish iron first — prerequisites not met
Start darbepoetin α at 60 µg/2 weekly
Transfuse one unit of packed RBCs
items.exp: Prerequisite to start EPO: TSAT ≥30% and s. ferritin ≥500 ng/ml (enough iron store) — both unmet here. (Book p810)

items.q: An anemic CKD patient with a history of completed stroke needs therapy. ESA status is:
items.exp: Absolute contraindication: stroke. (Book p810)
